subject: physics
question_text: A steel wire of length 20 cm and Poisson's ratio 0.19 is stretched so that its length increases by 0.2 cm. Find the lateral strain produced in the wire.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 9 Short Answer Question 5 (printed p.100). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The four-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: longitudinal strain = ΔL/L = 0.2/20 = 0.01; lateral strain = σ × longitudinal strain = 0.19 × 0.01 = 1.9 × 10⁻³. Matches the brief's independently checked arithmetic.

steps.label: Given data
lines: Length L = 20 cm, increase in length
steps.margin_note: Write down all three given values before starting the calculation.
steps.why: Poisson's ratio links two strains, so both the length data and the given ratio have to be on the page before either strain can be found.
common_mistakes: Starting the calculation without writing σ = 0.19 down first.
Confusing which value is the length and which is the extension.
steps.memory_tip: Three numbers to write down first: L, ΔL, and σ.

steps.label: Longitudinal strain
steps.margin_note: The unit cm cancels directly here, so no conversion to metres is needed.
steps.why: Longitudinal strain is the change in length over the original length, and since both are already in centimetres, the ratio needs no unit conversion.
common_mistakes: Converting to metres and making an arithmetic slip. 0.2 cm/20 cm is the same ratio as in any unit.
steps.memory_tip: 0.2 in 20 is the same as 1 in 100: longitudinal strain = 0.01.

steps.label: Poisson's ratio relation
lines: Poisson's ratio is the ratio of the
steps.margin_note: Rearranging the definition of σ to solve for the lateral strain is the whole of this mark.
steps.why: Poisson's ratio links the two strains directly, so once the longitudinal strain is known, this rearrangement gives the lateral strain in one step.
common_mistakes: Inverting the ratio and writing lateral strain = longitudinal strain / σ.
Leaving the relation in words only, without the rearranged formula.
steps.memory_tip: Lateral strain = σ × longitudinal strain: Poisson's ratio is the multiplier.

steps.label: Lateral strain
steps.margin_note: The value alone, with the correct power of ten, earns this mark.
steps.why: This step is a single multiplication of the two numbers found above, so the final answer follows directly once the relation in the previous step is written correctly.
common_mistakes: Misplacing the decimal and writing 1.9 × 10⁻² instead of 10⁻³.
Reporting a percentage instead of converting back to a plain ratio.
steps.memory_tip: 0.19 of a hundredth is about a fifth of a hundredth: 1.9 × 10⁻³.

insider_note: The whole answer is one multiplication once the longitudinal strain is found — most lost marks come from a misplaced decimal in the final power of ten.
